editorial:
Imagine living next to someone you absolutely cannot stand. That is exactly what happens here on a quiet little street where two men, Gormsen and Sandelund, are locked in a petty war that never seems to end. You have Gormsen, a dentist who loves communism and has a very young new wife, living in an old-style cottage. Then you have Sandelund, a meat dealer who loves money and lives in a flashy modern house with a flat roof. The vibe is a funny mix of political fighting and neighborly hate, with a local grocer named Krause caught in the middle. While the grown-ups act like children, their teenage kids are the only ones who realize how ridiculous the whole fight actually is.

What really works is how the movie shows the absurdity of these two men trying to outdo each other. The pacing is light, and watching Krause climb the social ladder while pretending to be a holy man is a highlight. If you like comedies that poke fun at social classes and ego, you will love this. Since it is an older film, you might want to look for a restored version.
endingExplained: The long war between the two neighbors finally reaches a breaking point where their hatred becomes totally pointless. After years of fighting over politics and house styles, they realize they are more alike than they thought. The movie wraps up by showing that their ego was the real enemy. Krause ends up as a successful businessman, and the teenagers' view of the world proves that the adults were just wasting their time with a silly feud.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quirky comedies about people who hate each other.
